# accumulator_map (Resource)

Accumulates `inputs` across applies into an `outputs` map keyed by the input keys. Every key ever seen is retained with its most recent value: re-supplying a key with a different value overwrites the stored value in place, and the key keeps its identity. A key is forgotten by a `triggers_reset` change, a replacement, or — when `expires_after` is set — expiry after the TTL; see `expires_after` for the clock rules. With `delayed_for` set, a newly supplied key lands in `accumulated` at once but joins `outputs` only after the delay; see `delayed_for` for the clock rules. A value change never delays or expires a key; only key presence matters.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "accumulator_map" "last_digest" {
  inputs        = { (var.service) = var.image_digest }
  delayed_for   = 600
  expires_after = 3600
}

output "last_digest" {
  value = accumulator_map.last_digest.outputs
}

output "last_digest_all" {
  value = accumulator_map.last_digest.accumulated
}

output "last_digest_detail" {
  value = accumulator_map.last_digest.detailed_outputs
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `inputs` (Map of String) The entries to accumulate. Terraform stores `inputs` in state so the value round-trips; an update merges it into `outputs` (or, when `triggers_reset` changes, reseeds `outputs` from it). A key already present takes the supplied value; re-supplying a key with the same value changes nothing.

### Optional

- `delayed_for` (Number) How many seconds a key waits in `accumulated` before it appears in `outputs`. The apply that first accumulates a key stamps its `visible_at` as now plus `delayed_for` and leaves it out of `outputs`; the reveal is realized at refresh: a key joins `outputs` when a refresh runs after its `visible_at` has passed, and running with `-refresh=false` defers the reveal until the next refresh. A late-applied saved plan will not reveal an entry even if the time has passed by the time the plan is applied — its refresh already ran at plan time; a new plan/apply is required. Create, replacement, and a `triggers_reset` change delay every seeded key. A value change on a key that is already present never delays it. Setting `delayed_for` on an existing resource hides nothing that is already visible. Changing the value recalculates every pending `visible_at` as min(old, new) on a decrease and max(old, new) on an increase; removing it reveals every pending key at that apply. Must be between 0 and 9223372036 (about 292 years) and strictly less than `expires_after` when both are set; `0` stamps the current moment so the next refresh reveals the key. Leave it null to disable the delay entirely.
- `expires_after` (Number) How many seconds a key that has left `inputs` survives in `outputs`. While a key stays in `inputs` it never expires and its `expires_at` is null, whatever happens to its value. Expiration is realized at refresh: a key is removed when a refresh runs after its `expires_at` has passed, and running with `-refresh=false` defers removal until the next refresh. A late-applied saved plan will not expire an entry even if the time has passed by the time the plan is applied — its refresh already ran at plan time; a new plan/apply is required. The entry for a key that leaves `inputs` (or whose stamp is being recalculated after an `expires_after` change) shows as known after apply in that apply's plan. Changing the value recalculates every existing `expires_at` as min(old, new) on a decrease and max(old, new) on an increase. Must be between 0 and 9223372036 (about 292 years); `0` stamps a key with the current moment as it leaves `inputs`, so the next refresh removes it. Leave it null to disable expiration entirely.
- `triggers_replacement` (String) Change this value to force a replacement (destroy and recreate), which reseeds `outputs` from `inputs`. Any change counts, including from null to a value. Leave it null for no replacement.
- `triggers_reset` (String) Change this value to discard the accumulated map and reseed `outputs` from `inputs`, forgetting every key seen before the change. Any change counts, including from null to a value. Leave it null for no reset.

### Read-Only

- `accumulated` (Map of String) Every key ever accumulated with its most recent value, including keys still waiting out `delayed_for`. `outputs` is this map minus the pending keys; with `delayed_for` null the two are always equal. Computed; never configured. Known at plan time under the same conditions as `outputs`.
- `detailed_outputs` (Map of Object) A map from every key in `accumulated` to its timing attributes. `expires_at` is an RFC 3339 timestamp of when the key will be removed, or null when the key cannot expire: it is in `inputs`, or `expires_after` is null. `visible_at` is an RFC 3339 timestamp of when a pending key will join `outputs`, or null when it is already visible. Computed; never configured. Entries being stamped by an apply show as known after apply in that apply's plan. Expiry and reveal are realized at refresh; a late-applied saved plan will not expire or reveal an entry whose time passed after the plan was created — a new plan/apply is required. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--detailed_outputs))
- `id` (String) A stable identifier: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the canonical JSON encoding of the resource's initial values. On create (and replacement) that is the `inputs` map; on import it is the seeded `outputs`, because a map resource seeds no meaningful `inputs`. Stable across in-place updates.
- `outputs` (Map of String) The visible entries: `accumulated` minus every key still waiting out `delayed_for`, values carried verbatim. Computed; never configured. The plan shows the value the next apply will produce, computed against the prior state. When `inputs` (including any single entry's value), a trigger, `expires_after`, or `delayed_for` is itself unknown at plan time, `outputs` plans as unknown and the apply resolves it.

### Nested Schema for `detailed_outputs`

Read-Only:

- `expires_at` (String)
- `visible_at` (String)

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# accumulator_map seeds outputs from a JSON object of strings and hashes it
# for id. An inputs key, if present, is accepted and ignored: inputs is
# seeded as an empty map, and the first plan after import supplies it from
# configuration and merges it into the seeded outputs.
terraform import accumulator_map.last_digest '{"outputs":{"api":"sha256:ab","web":"sha256:cd"}}'
```
